title: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370
wiki_lead:
Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 (MH370 / MAS370) was an international passenger flight from Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia to Beijing Capital International Airport in China. On 8 March 2014, the Boeing 777 operating on the route disappeared from radar with 227 passengers and 12 crew members on board. Although the cause of its disapperance has been inconclusive, the aircraft was diverted manually but it is unknown who was responsible or why. It is widely regarded as the greatest mystery in aviation history.
The crew of the aircraft last communicated with air traffic control (ATC) around 38 minutes after takeoff while flying over the South China Sea. The aircraft was lost from ATC's secondary surveillance radar screens minutes later, but was tracked by the Malaysian military's primary radar system for another hour as it manually deviated westward from its planned flight path. It left radar range 200 nautical miles (370 km; 230 mi) west-northwest of Penang Island in northwestern Peninsular Malaysia.
Relying mostly on the analysis of data from the Inmarsat satellite with which the aircraft last communicated, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) initially proposed that a hypoxia event was the most likely cause given the available evidence, although no consensus has been reached among investigators concerning this theory. At various stages of the investigation, possible hijacking scenarios were considered, including crew involvement, and suspicion of the aircraft's cargo manifest. Many disappearance theories regarding the flight have also been reported by the media.
With all 227 passengers and 12 crew aboard presumed dead, the disappearance of Flight 370 was the deadliest incident involving a Boeing 777, the deadliest of 2014, and the deadliest in Malaysia Airlines' history until it was surpassed in all three regards by Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 on 17 July 2014. 
The search for the missing aircraft became the most expensive search in aviation history at US$135–160 million. It focused initially on the South China Sea and Andaman Sea, before a novel analysis of the aircraft's automated communications with an Inmarsat satellite indicated that the aircraft had travelled far southward over the southern Indian Ocean. Several pieces of debris washed ashore in the western Indian Ocean during 2015 and 2016; many of these were confirmed to have originated from Flight 370. After a three-year search across 120,000 km2 (46,000 sq mi) of ocean failed to locate the aircraft, the Joint Agency Coordination Centre heading the operation suspended its activities in January 2017. A second search launched in January 2018 by private contractor Ocean Infinity also ended without success after six months. The Malaysian Ministry of Transport's final report from July 2018 was inconclusive.
In the absence of a definitive cause of disappearance, air transport industry safety recommendations and regulations citing Flight 370 have been implemented to prevent a repetition of the circumstances associated with the loss. These include increased battery life on underwater locator beacons, lengthening of recording times on flight data recorders and cockpit voice recorders, and new standards for aircraft position reporting over open ocean.

grok_lead: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 (MH370) was a Boeing 777-200ER scheduled to carry 227 passengers and 12 crew from Kuala Lumpur International Airport to Beijing Capital International Airport when it disappeared on 8 March 2014 shortly after takeoff at 00:41 MYT. The aircraft lost contact with air traffic control over the South China Sea near waypoint IGARI, after which its transponder was disabled and it deviated sharply from its planned northeast route, turning back westward across the Malay Peninsula as tracked by Malaysian military primary radar. Subsequent analysis of automated satellite "handshake" pings from Inmarsat indicated the plane continued flying for about seven hours, arcing southward into the remote southeastern Indian Ocean where it likely exhausted its fuel and crashed, based on Doppler shift and elapsed time calculations validated against known flight paths. An extensive multinational search, led initially by Malaysia and later focused in the Indian Ocean by Australia, scanned more than 230,000 square kilometers of seabed using sonar and submersibles (with the total underwater search area approaching 250,000 square kilometers by 2026) but yielded no main wreckage or flight recorders, hampered by the vast, deep terrain and imprecise endpoint estimates from the satellite data. The most recent Ocean Infinity campaign, conducted in two phases from March 2025 to January 2026 and covering approximately 7,571 square kilometers of a planned 15,000-square-kilometer area, found no confirmed wreckage. Several pieces of debris, including a confirmed flaperon from the right wing found on RÃ©union Island in 2015 and two other wing fragments positively identified as from MH370, along with additional fragments assessed as almost certainly matching via serial numbers and barnacle analysis, drifted ashore on African and Indian Ocean coasts, consistent with ocean currents from a southern crash site but providing limited causal insight. The official Malaysian investigation concluded the deviations required manual intervention inconsistent with autopilot modes, ruling out mechanical failure or fire as primary causes, yet could not identify perpetrators or motives amid conflicting theories ranging from pilot action to external interference, underscoring gaps in aviation tracking and response protocols.
